title: Firefighter Salary WA: Converting Hourly to Annual Pay with Tax and Super
description: Learn how to convert a firefighter salary WA hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. Includes tax, Medicare, and super estimates based on 38-hour weeks.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is the hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52; super is paid on top at 12%.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly firefighter salary in WA to an annual figure?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. If you work a standard 38-hour week, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual pay before tax and super. Super is paid on top of this amount.

faqs.q: What tax and Medicare levy apply to a firefighter salary in WA?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, resident tax rates are: nil up to $18,200, 15% from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. These are deducted from your gross annual pay to estimate take-home pay.

faqs.q: Does the average weekly earnings figure for WA apply to firefighters?
faqs.a: No. The ABS average full‑time ordinary time earnings for Western Australia is $2,227.40 per week (May 2026), but that is an average across all occupations, not a median or typical figure for firefighters. Firefighters may be covered by specific awards or enterprise agreements that set different rates.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate and Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage, converting it to an annual salary helps you compare job offers or plan your budget. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38‑hour week, which is the full‑time ordinary hours under the Fair Work Act. If you work different hours, adjust the calculation accordingly. For example, a 40‑hour week would use 40 instead of 38.

Knowing your annual figure also lets you work out your fortnightly pay (weekly pay × 2) and your weekly pay (hourly × hours per week).

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, many occupations are covered by awards or enterprise agreements that set higher minimum rates. Always check the relevant award or agreement for your role.

If you are a casual worker, use the checkbox on [the timesheet](/) to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading.

## Tax and Medicare on Your Annual Figure

Once you have your gross annual pay, you can estimate the tax and Medicare levy you will owe as a resident for 2026–27. The Australian Taxation Office uses these tax brackets:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of the excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% of the excess over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate. The levy may be reduced for low‑income earners.

These deductions are subtracted from your gross annual pay to give an estimate of your take‑home pay. For a more detailed breakdown, see our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your gross pay. It is not deducted from your hourly rate or annual salary. The super contribution is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). If your ordinary earnings exceed that amount, super is only paid on the first $270,830.

For example, if your annual gross pay is $80,000, your employer would contribute $9,600 (12%) to your super fund. This amount is in addition to your salary, not part of it. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Firefighter Salary WA: A Contextual Reference

When researching a firefighter salary in Western Australia, you may come across the ABS Average Weekly Earnings figure for the state. For May 2026, full‑time adult ordinary time earnings in WA were $2,227.40 per week. This is an average across all occupations and industries, not a median or a specific figure for firefighters. Firefighters in WA are likely covered by the Fire and Rescue NSW Award or a similar state‑based industrial instrument, which sets minimum rates, allowances, and penalty rates. For accurate information, refer to the relevant [pay guides](/blog) or your enterprise agreement.

To estimate your own firefighter salary WA, start with your hourly rate (including any allowances or penalties if they are guaranteed) and use the formula above. Remember that overtime, shift penalties, and allowances are not included in this basic conversion.

## Using the Timesheet for Your Own Calculation

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and, if applicable, check the casual loading box. It will then calculate your annual, fortnightly, weekly, and monthly gross pay, plus estimated tax, Medicare levy, and super. You can also view [reference tables](/data) for common rates and thresholds.

This tool is an estimate only. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. Always consult a qualified professional for personal financial advice.
